compiled_state.description:
The mcp service in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` does not set `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL`.
On a fresh deploy the container crash-loops before serving: `AuthSettings` (pydantic) raises a
ValidationError because `issuer_url` is empty (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py` ~L609,
`AuthSettings(issuer_url=mcp_cfg.auth_issuer_url, ...)`), and `/health` never comes up.

## Root cause (surfaced by jackal live deploy)
The compose mcp `environment:` block sets `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_RESOURCE_SERVER_URL` (compose ~L347)
but omits the sibling `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL`. `fetch-secrets.sh` does not inject it either,
so the container boots with an empty issuer URL and fails auth-settings construction.

## Live impact
On the prod box the endpoint only came up after a temporary `.env` hotfix appending
`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL=https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`. Autodeploy rsync from main
will drop that hotfix and can re-crash the mcp container on the next blue-green tick.

## Fix
Add to the mcp `environment:` block, mirroring how RESOURCE_SERVER_URL is set:
`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL: "${REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL:-https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp}"`

## RED-first oracle
A compose-assertion test that parses docker-compose.yml and asserts the mcp service environment
defines a non-empty `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL` (fails today, passes after the fix). Note:
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth.py` always sets `auth_issuer_url` explicitly, so unit
tests never caught the compose omission — the gap is deploy config, not the auth code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RED compose-assertion test proves the mcp service env omits a non-empty issuer URL, then passes after the fix.
- [ ] docker-compose.yml mcp environment sets REBAR_MCP_AUTH_ISSUER_URL (default to the prod /mcp URL, overridable).
- [ ] Lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1).
